text.p: - President Boris Yeltsin's press-secretary has announced the decision to relieve former Kremlin security chief Alexander Korzhakov of his military duties. Technically, it will not be easy to implement.

- The presidential administration has undertaken to create a clear-cut structure of executive power which should be free of internal contradictions. The president's chief-of-staff, Anatoly Chubais, is apparently playing the role of the strongman which was played until recently by Alexander Lebed.

- The government's emergency tax commission has outlined its main aims and what it covers -- bankruptcy, cracking down on capital flight and improving tax collection. But it is not clear how the commission will achieve its goal and the effect of the measures will be.
- The Kremlin has declared war on the president's former security chif Alexander Korzhakov. The president's administration must have found some compromising materials against the general.

- Russia's new Security Council secretary, Ivan Rybkin, has paid a visit to the North Caucasus where he met with some Chechen opposition leaders. The results of this trip were not exciting, both parties were just getting to know each other.

- An opinion poll conducted in the town of Tula in central Russia suggests that Alexander Korzhakov has a poor chance of winning a seat in the State Duma lower house of the parliament in the local election there, says the newspaper, which has links with the president's administration.
- The south of Russia has voted for leftist forces, the paper says in a comment on regional elections.
- The president will come back, Kremlin chief doctor Sergei Mironov says in an interview with the newspaper.
